A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPHERE and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. The framework, tasks, experiments, and appendix material can be matched despite retitling and expanded model comparisons.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM accuracy and validity measurements, viewpoint comparisons, fact-assisted reasoning experiments, and dataset analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports expanded VLM evaluations, human-baseline scores, retained diagnostic experiments, and additional dataset analysis in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: SPHERE retains its three-level hierarchy, nine tasks, intermediate-question decomposition, and ground-truth-assisted prompting procedure. Additional evaluated models and annotation explanations do not introduce a new proposed algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Both versions use static MS COCO-2017 test images for the same spatial tasks and overall allocentric/egocentric coverage. Revisions to question counts and annotation distributions do not establish an added domain or distinct task.

E2.justification: The eight evaluated model configurations expand to seventeen, adding LLaVA-OneVision, Qwen2-VL (7B/72B), InternVL2.5, Llama-3.2-Vision (11B/90B), Gemini 2.0 Flash, GPT-4o, and SpatialRGPT-RGB. A human baseline is added. Random-baseline entries disappear from the detailed viewpoint and reasoning tables, although retained in the main comparison.

E3.justification: The dataset decreases from 2,288 to 2,285 questions: Position + Counting changes from 65/107 egocentric/allocentric questions to 64/105. Annotation distributions also change slightly. v2 adds larger model configurations and overall score summaries, while retaining the accuracy/validity definitions and diagnostic prompting procedure. The human-testing protocol and causes of retained-model score revisions are unspecified.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds an object-concept diversity analysis, reporting over 600 concepts and plotting the top 30 in Figure 10. The viewpoint, intermediate-versus-final, and supplied-fact analyses remain and are extended to additional models; their underlying diagnostic questions are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five evaluations per question using different seeds and report averaged accuracy/validity. Appendix A retains negative-binomial fitting and Pearson chi-square tests. Changed test statistics and p-values are result updates, without a changed uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Accuracy, validity, and diagnostic results are extensively revised and expanded. For example, LLaVA-NeXT Counting changes from 56.7% in v1 Table 2 to 68.7% in v2 Table 3. New overall scores include GPT-4o at 67.9% and humans at 93.0%. Appendix distributions and goodness-of-fit values also change. These are reported revisions, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised. The benchmark definitions and random-guessing formula remain unchanged; appendix additions concern empirical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the evaluation claim from open-source VLMs to state-of-the-art VLMs generally, consistent with adding proprietary models. The hierarchical benchmark contribution and central claims about spatial weaknesses remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains that pairing only two skills reduces confounding and adds that automatic annotation may become viable as VLMs improve. It removes v1's blanket characterization that supplied facts never raise reasoning accuracy above 60%. The size-constancy interpretation and static-image/scope limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents replacing inconsistent annotations, spaCy en_core_web_sm noun extraction and manual filtering, and the RGB-only SpatialRGPT choice. It removes the SpaceMantis fine-tuning provenance explanation. The hardware statement, released-implementation guidance, and promised dataset release upon publication remain.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds SEED-Bench and MM-Vet as examples with limited spatial-task coverage, and references supporting newly evaluated models are added. The central positioning against existing spatial benchmarks remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, an author and affiliation are added, and the results narrative is updated. Main-text validity discussion is shortened while detailed discussion remains in Appendix B. Section order and most framework/task explanations are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a first-page ranking table and Figure 10, transposes and expands the four model-result tables, introduces overall columns, and highlights rankings in the accuracy and viewpoint tables. Several displays are relocated. This substantially redesigns the presentation of empirical evidence.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons test whether spatial weaknesses persist in stronger open and proprietary models, addressing v1's narrow empirical base. Object-diversity analysis and redesigned tables also improve the paper's usefulness. However, the missing human-baseline protocol and unexplained revisions to many retained-model scores limit the confidence added by the expanded evidence.
